Container.Name: Noxa
Container.Overview: Noxa is a lightweight, self-hosted media server for your movies, TV shows, anime and photos. It plays files directly whenever it can and only transcodes when a client needs it, with optional hardware acceleration (Intel / AMD VAAPI, NVIDIA). No account, no telemetry. Clients: web browser, Android TV, Android and desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux). Also: linked servers (share catalogues and accounts between Noxa servers), cold storage for titles you rarely watch, a photo library and a DLNA server.[br][br]After the first start, open the web UI: it asks for the setup code shown in the container log.
Container.Requires: For hardware transcoding with Intel or AMD, pass /dev/dri (below). With NVIDIA, install the Nvidia Driver plugin and add --runtime=nvidia to Extra Parameters, with the NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES variable.

Config.Name: Linked servers port
Config.Description: TLS port for linked servers. Only needed if another Noxa server must reach this one.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database, image and subtitle cache, settings.

Config.Name: Movies
Config.Description: Your movies (read only). In Noxa, add a library pointing to /media/movies.

Config.Name: TV shows
Config.Description: Your TV shows and anime (read only). In Noxa, add a library pointing to /media/shows.

Config.Name: Photos
Config.Description: Optional photo library (read only), added in Noxa as a Photos library pointing to /media/photos.

Config.Name: Intel / AMD GPU
Config.Description: Optional: hardware transcoding with VAAPI. Leave empty if you have no GPU.

Config.Name: Secure cookies
Config.Description: Set to 1 when Noxa is reached through an HTTPS reverse proxy.

Config.Name: Trust proxy
Config.Description: Set to 1 behind a reverse proxy, so Noxa sees the real client IP.
